scope: Proposition 3.1 (Multipoint radius estimate) of the manuscript “An exact Hausdorff gauge for SLE” (preprints/An-exact-Hausdorff-gauge-for-SLE-September-25-2026/An-exact-Hausdorff-gauge-for-SLE-September-25-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 230 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 513ca9aedce0f342), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let D = J(H) as in Section 2, and let x1, . . . , xm ∈ D be distinct. Suppose 0 < bi ≤ RD(xi), bi ≤ |xi − xj| (j ̸= i). For targets 0 < ei ≤ bi, let E be the event that each xi reaches conformal radius ei while alive. Then P(E) ≤ Cm,a m ∏︂ i=1 (ei/bi)α . (3.1) The constant depends only on m and a, independently of D, J, the initial angles, the radii, and the order and times of the hits. A point need not remain alive after reaching its own target. For targets exceeding some caps, the corresponding constraints may be dropped, giving, after enlarging Cm,a, P(E) ≤ Cm,a m ∏︂ i=1 min{1, (ei/bi)α }. (3.2)
